summary: The PR-168 exact-mechanics claim boundary passes direct supplemental review: result-card and theorem values agree, negative controls delimit the identity, the rendered figure has only shear and vorticity curves, its bytes match the sidecar, and restricted claim lint is clean. Closeout provenance does not pass. The generated theorem signature lacks the repository-mandated standalone artifact metadata, and the PR delta's Verification section contains no exact commands or pass/fail/skip outcomes. A lower-severity figure-label issue leaves the geodesic domain of the vorticity curve implicit rather than visible in the legend or explicit in the sidecar caveats.

findings.title: The generated theorem signature is not standalone provenance-complete
findings.symptom: docs/generated/pr168_theorem_signature.json is a generated, manifest-bound claim artifact, but it carries none of owner, implementation_scope, claim_tier, transfer_source, config_hash, input_hashes, sky_support_mask_status, covariance_null_mock_status, caveats, generating_command, or git_commit_or_worktree_state. It also lacks artifact_mode, public_use, and typed allowed_uses/forbidden_uses. evidence_hashes and forbidden_promotions provide useful content but do not supply the missing ownership, lane, generation, and environment fields.
findings.source: The theorem-signature schema records the mathematical statement and CAS evidence but does not implement the repository's minimum per-artifact metadata contract.
findings.consequence: A copied or separately consumed theorem signature cannot be routed to COMMON, constrained to conditional_exact_mechanics/internal use, tied to a generating command/worktree, or automatically quarantined from observational/transfer/family promotion without relying on an external wrapper. That violates the rule that every result artifact carry its own claim and provenance lane.
findings.remediation: Extend htt.pr168.theorem_signature.v1 or version it to include the full minimum metadata block. Populate owner=COMMON, the exact implementation scope, claim tier/level, artifact mode/public-use and allowed/forbidden-use fields, transfer/config/input hashes, not-applicable sky/null fields, caveats, generating command, runtime, and Git state; then regenerate and rebind every parent hash.
findings.reproducible_check: Compare the theorem-signature top-level keys with the eleven minimum metadata keys; all eleven are absent, while the result card and figure sidecar have zero missing minimum keys.

findings.title: The PR delta does not record the exact verification bundle or outcomes
findings.symptom: The Verification section says that targeted, DAG/mirror, smoke, claim-language, manuscript-build, scientific-code-validation, and independent-review checks are or will be recorded, but it provides no executable command, collected/executed/passed counts, pass/fail status, skips, failures, artifact hashes, or review-envelope paths.
findings.source: The delta uses a prose coverage promise in place of the evidence record required by the per-PR loop.
findings.consequence: An external reviewer cannot reproduce the claimed closeout, distinguish already-passing gates from future work, or verify that optional skips and failures were not hidden. The delta therefore cannot support a terminal PR-168 status even though the scoped claim content is correctly downclaimed.
findings.remediation: Replace the Verification paragraph with the exact command list and outcomes for the governing targeted suite, DAG/mirror validation, smoke, claim lint, manuscript build, scientific-code validation, mutation closeout, and each independent review. Include counts, skipped/failed reasons, artifact/result paths plus hashes, and the final worktree/commit binding. Do not use future tense for completed evidence.
findings.reproducible_check: A targeted search of the delta for python, pytest, make, PASS, FAIL, SKIP, passed, collected, and command returns no lines.

findings.title: The two-bound figure leaves the vorticity curve's geodesic domain implicit
findings.symptom: The rendered legend labels the orange curve only as B_omega (vorticity). The sidecar says that registered shear/vorticity consumer semantics are preserved and that no non-geodesic acceleration ceiling is plotted, but it never explicitly says that B_omega is the geodesic vorticity combination. The image itself has no geodesic or unavailable-acceleration annotation.
findings.source: The generator removed the acceleration curve but retained a shortened legacy legend and a generic sidecar caveat.
findings.consequence: When the PNG is viewed apart from its manuscript paragraph, the vorticity line can be mistaken for an unrestricted MES vorticity bound. public_use=false limits exposure, but the figure is still less self-contained than the PR-168 domain split requires.
findings.remediation: Label the legend B_omega (vorticity, geodesic) and add an explicit sidecar caveat that the non-geodesic vorticity/acceleration ceiling is unavailable and no acceleration curve exists. Keep public_use=false and rebind the image and sidecar hashes.

claim_results.reason: The exact result is consistently restricted to aligned-scalar, thermodynamic-temperature, first-order, homogeneous k_eff=0, fixed-operator mechanics. The result card and theorem exact-result objects match, their forbidden-promotion lists match, and finite-k/operator/second-order negative controls are nonzero. The active non-geodesic ceiling is typed unavailable with numeric=null and numeric_allowed=false. The image contains only two curves and matches its sidecar hash. Closeout nevertheless fails on missing theorem-signature metadata and a non-evidentiary delta verification record.
claim_results.kill_switch: Any remediation that changes the exact result, treats CAS agreement as an independent covariant derivation, adds a third acceleration curve, substitutes geodesic zero for a universal non-geodesic ceiling, or promotes the identity to finite-k, full-transfer, observational, geometry, or family equivalence is a hard fail.
